competitive_position.vs_samsung: HBM3e yield advantage, NVIDIA supply share ~52% vs Samsung ~35%
competitive_position.vs_micron: 2-generation lead in HBM; Micron at ~13% share, still on HBM3e
competitive_position.moat: CoWoS packaging relationship with TSMC + NVIDIA qualification lead time

scm_engagement.scm_role: World's #1 HBM supplier. Manufactures the high-bandwidth memory stacks that are bonded directly onto NVIDIA/AMD AI GPU dies via TSMC CoWoS packaging. Without SK Hynix HBM, NVIDIA cannot ship H200 or B200 GPUs.

server_products.name: HBM3e 24GB Stack (8-Hi)
server_products.note: 12 stacks per H200 GPU (141GB total). SK Hynix supplies ~52% of all HBM to NVIDIA.

server_products.name: HBM3e 24GB Stack (12-Hi)
server_products.note: 16 stacks per B200 GPU (192GB total). GB200 NVL72 rack = 72 GPUs = 13.8TB HBM.

server_products.name: HBM4 32GB Stack (target)
server_products.note: Mass production expected H2 2026. Qualification race with Micron.

server_products.name: DDR5 Server DRAM
server_products.used_in: AI server CPU DRAM slots (Intel Xeon, AMD EPYC hosts)
server_products.note: All AI servers need host DRAM for OS, data pipelines, model orchestration.

scm_engagement.scm_position: Memory tier — bonded onto GPU die at TSMC CoWoS

lead_time.description: HBM wafer-out → tokens served ≈ 12 months under normal conditions. TSMC CoWoS slot is the rate-limiter (18-month capacity lead time for new capacity).
lead_time.bottleneck: TSMC CoWoS packaging slot — 18-month lead for new capacity additions
